hypothesis: Typed relational causal-state nodes plus action-conditioned recurrent 1-5 step dynamics improve task-disjoint next-action and free-rollout prediction over Structured Markov v3 plus MLP.
interpretation: Raw typed lexical nodes overfit task identity and badly degrade one-step transfer; multi-horizon supervision is directionally useful at horizons 3-5 and should only be reused as a residual attached to the retained structured baseline.

hypothesis: A trajectory-normalized four-cell task/attack auxiliary cross-entropy improves the unchanged Structured Markov v3 dynamics and learns joint outcome probabilities beyond the training-task prior.
interpretation: The auxiliary provides a transferable outcome regularizer: next-action NLL and accuracy improve while joint CE/Brier beat the task-fold prior; observable outcome BCE remains within noninferiority.

hypothesis: A zero-initialized recurrent residual over the retained Structured Markov plus four-cell teacher preserves task-disjoint one-step performance while adding transferable 2-5 step rollout capacity without raw typed text nodes.
interpretation: The conservative residual retains the original Structured Markov one-step gain and beats typed v4 on every held-out task at horizons 2-5. It is the leading world-model candidate, but v5 remains fractionally better at h1 and fresh Structured-only rollout controls are still required for a general-superiority claim.

hypothesis: Canonical relational slots add transferable state information to v6 without raw-text task memorization.
interpretation: The slots preserve h1 and pass all integrity checks but slightly worsen multi-step and future-joint prediction; downstream supervision alone does not make the anonymized slots useful.

hypothesis: EMA-target action-conditioned JEPA plus semantic grounding turns canonical relational slots into a transferable predictive latent.
interpretation: JEPA prevents collapse and improves future four-cell CE, but worsens h2-h5 in every seed. Predictive regularization cannot recover domain intent content removed by the anonymized slot builder.

hypothesis: Interface-aligned concept/tool affordances restore transferable domain intent omitted by v7 while retaining a strict lexical bottleneck.
interpretation: The bottleneck repairs Travel multi-step signal and preserves h1, but downstream rollout losses do not produce broad multi-step transfer; direct successor-action supervision is authorized.

hypothesis: A discounted successor-action occupancy objective makes affordance slots predict future tool demand directly.
interpretation: Successor supervision improves C1 and preserves the Travel repair, but does not beat v6, fails seed replication, and violates h1 accuracy noninferiority. Pure replacement is not authorized.

hypothesis: Four deterministic track-routed adapters over a shared interface-affordance encoder prevent cross-domain gradient interference and outperform a parameter-matched dense adapter.
interpretation: The task-ID-free router and parameter match are valid, but coarse domain experts worsen h2-h5 NLL versus both v6 and the dense control, sharply degrade Slack, and also fail h1-accuracy and future-joint noninferiority. Pure latent replacement is not authorized.

hypothesis: A non-lexical relation-state signature with top-2 dynamic basis residuals removes coarse-domain interference and beats v6 and a parameter-matched dense control.
interpretation: The relation signature improves future four-cell CE and repairs Travel, but sparse routing is slightly worse than v6 and the identical-input dense control, retains Slack degradation, and has insufficient routing entropy. The latent-router direction is stopped and the frozen uncertainty direction switch is authorized.

hypothesis: A uniform three-member v6 ensemble improves task-disjoint predictive distributions and separates epistemic model error after the latent-router direction fails.
interpretation: Uniform ensembling improves h1 NLL and future-joint CE on every task and yields a small universal multi-step NLL gain, but loses h1 accuracy, misses the required multi-step effect size, and does not reliably separate errors by epistemic disagreement. Keep it only as a calibration diagnostic and redirect future work to explicit semantic transition targets.

hypothesis: Predicting causal observation, evidence, goal-progress, and execution factors before conditioning a zero-initialized residual improves task-disjoint next-action and free-rollout prediction over v6.
interpretation: Evidence and execution factors transfer, but generic observation and progress factors do not; predicted v11 worsens h2-h5 and future four-cell CE, and true oracle factors do not repair the deficit. The bottleneck is factor usefulness rather than encoder capacity. Retain v6 and switch to an oracle-first action-conditioned event-graph target study.

hypothesis: True causal action/tool/argument/receipt event graphs are sufficient to improve task-disjoint action rollout and future joint outcomes over v6 before learning a graph predictor.
interpretation: Event graphs strongly improve h2-h5 action NLL over v6 and an equal-capacity zero-graph control on 18/20 tasks and all seeds, but shared graph conditioning degrades future four-cell CE. The shared-hidden model is rejected; the action signal is retained only as mechanism evidence for a new modular dynamics/outcome split.

hypothesis: Separating the event-graph action branch from the four-cell outcome branch removes v12 shared-hidden negative transfer.
interpretation: Exact same-key recombination retains the v12 h2-h5 action gain and copies v6 outcomes exactly, proving modular separation is sufficient to eliminate the observed negative transfer and authorizing a causal graph predictor.

hypothesis: A causal learned event-graph predictor can replace the v12 true-graph oracle while an independent frozen v6 branch preserves four-cell outcomes.
interpretation: The full graph is not predictable under task-disjoint transfer: its unweighted BCE is worse than the training-fold prior in every seed. Predicted graphs fail to retain the oracle multi-step gain. Keep modular outcome separation, reject dense full-graph reconstruction, and switch to exact action/tool structure plus learned stochastic receipt/evidence residuals.

hypothesis: The v12 full event graph gain is attributable independently to exact action/tool protocol structure or to stochastic receipt/evidence residuals.
interpretation: The full modular graph reproduces the strong multi-step gain. Exact and evidence partitions are each broad and seed-replicated, but neither clears every frozen threshold; evidence retains 69.7% versus the required 70%. The result identifies an exact-by-evidence interaction and authorizes late-fusion action-relevant distillation, not dense graph reconstruction.

hypothesis: A zero-initialized exact/evidence late-fusion student can retain full-graph action dynamics by distilling oracle action distributions instead of reconstructing sparse future graphs.
interpretation: Distillation improves oracle imitation and beats an equal-capacity control, but free-running h2-h5 performance is worse than v6 in every seed. The target depends on true future evidence unavailable to the student. Stop neural latent generation and switch to retrieval-grounded transition prototypes with explicit coverage uncertainty.

hypothesis: Task-disjoint semantic transition prototypes provide reliable successor-action forecasts on coverage-calibrated held-out events.
interpretation: Retrieval covers 85% of multi-step rows and similarity ranks errors, but even supported forecasts are much worse than v6 on 19/20 tasks and all seeds. Semantic proximity is not causal task-obligation equivalence. Stop architecture search on the observational dataset and switch to clean counterfactual branching data.

hypothesis: Four outcome-blind legal actions from each exact clean prefix provide reproducible and non-trivial action-effect supervision including boundary events.
interpretation: All 12 roots yielded at least three effects and 95.83% of same-root pairs differed, proving ordinary action effects are identifiable. Only three ambiguities and no errors or conflicts occurred, so the frozen broad gate fails. Switch from clean-donor action selection to paired parameter interventions and later modify-readback forks.

hypothesis: One-field schema-valid parameter interventions at the same reconstructed state and tool expose reproducible execution boundaries absent from clean donor actions.
interpretation: All 12 valid controls succeeded and all 12 matched corruptions flipped to deterministic errors with changed successor effects across all four suites. Retain parameter interventions as a paired data component, but require modify-readback persistence and legal-conflict evidence before any learned world-model comparison.

hypothesis: Same-root successful writes persist into repeated readback and a second legal write creates a reproducible model-visible successor difference across all four AgentDojo suites.
interpretation: All 24 sequences and 12 task pairs passed: shared first writes were identical, both persistence and competing-update expectations matched, and every final semantic state and observation differed. Freeze a grouped v17+v18+v19 union and authorize one tiny task-disjoint modular world-model comparison; attacks and large training remain unauthorized.
